validation_obligations.title: Bounded instruction representation: only .b32 is representable

validation_obligations.title: B32 values are within the 32-bit .b32 domain by representation (PRF-6 disposition)

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish that the execution relation XorB32Step is deterministic: for any state s and instruction i, at most one resulting state is related. This is the derived determinism interpretation PTX-XOR-SEM1-047 (determinism NOT explicitly stated in the source, bundle GAP-3), realized non-vacuously over the relational semantics per design D-25 / PTX-XOR-SEM1-063. Because XorB32Step is a Prop-valued inductive relation and not a function, the theorem is not a definitional triviality: it must rule out the possibility that both the guardFalse and executed constructors (or two executions) relate distinct resulting states.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every machine state s, instruction i, and states s1, s2: if XorB32Step s i s1 and XorB32Step s i s2, then s1 = s2.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem xorB32Step_deterministic
    (s : MachineState) (i : XorB32Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState)
    (h1 : XorB32Step s i s1) (h2 : XorB32Step s i s2) :
    s1 = s2
hypotheses: h1 : XorB32Step s i s1 (the relation admits a step from s on i to s1)
h2 : XorB32Step s i s2 (the relation admits a step from s on i to s2)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: s1 = s2 (at most one resulting state).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Derived interpretation PTX-XOR-SEM1-047 (determinism; GAP-3, not explicitly stated in the source); design dependency PTX-XOR-SEM1-063 (D-25 relational representation so that determinism is non-vacuous); design dependency PTX-XOR-SEM1-064 (two-case outcome executed/guardFalse, no error constructor). Source evidence: PTX-9.3-XOR-002 ('Bitwise exclusive-OR (inequality).'), PTX-9.3-XOR-004 ('Compute the bit-wise exclusive-or operation for the bits in a and b.'), PTX-9.3-XOR-005 ('d = a ^ b;'), PTX-9.3-XOR-018 (guard evaluation). No arithmetic-result assumption is involved because the exclusive-or is a pure bit-wise operation over two fixed 32-bit values.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The relation is inhabited: the executable example with r1 = 5, r2 = 3 and unguarded xor.b32 r1, r1, r2 (aliasing d == a, demonstrated by #eval: r1 becomes 5 ^ 3 = 6) yields a XorB32Step from the executed constructor; the @p with p = false example (r1 stays 5) yields a XorB32Step from the guardFalse constructor. The conclusion s1 = s2 is not an element of the hypotheses; the theorem excludes a hypothetical relation that admitted two distinct results. This is the meaningful relational determinism property required by D-25; the trivial single-valuedness of the total function execXorB32 is NOT this obligation (see traceability_summary.determinism_note).
strength_risks: The theorem must not be misread as functional totality of execXorB32; it is a relational property over XorB32Step only.

The proof is a short case analysis on the two constructors using disjointness of evalGuard outcomes (some false vs some true) and is appropriate; the reviewer should confirm the statement adds no unapproved totality or totality-on-well-formed-domain precondition.
The theorem does not assert existence of a step (that is a completeness/correspondence matter, PTX-XOR-THM-002); it asserts uniqueness when a step exists.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case on h1 and h2. If both come from the guardFalse constructor, the conclusion is reflexivity (s1 = s and s2 = s). If both come from the executed constructor, both give the same post-state updateDestination s i.d (xorValue va vb) with (possibly) different va/vb values, but each constructor premise fixes evalSource s i.a and evalSource s i.b to the respective values, so injectivity of some (Option) yields va1 = va2 and vb1 = vb2 (the result value xorValue va vb is then equal by congruence). If one is guardFalse and the other executed, the premises force evalGuard s i.guard = some false and evalGuard s i.guard = some true respectively, contradicting the disjointness of the two Option Bool values; derive False.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-1 (determinism of the execution relation).

theorem_obligations.category: function/relation correspondence (PRF-1 family; Lean file deferred item)
theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the correspondence between the executable function execXorB32 and the relational semantics XorB32Step. This is the item explicitly deferred by the Lean mapping itself (XorB32-v1.lean lines 305-316: 'The correspondence between the relation and the executable function is a theorem-stage obligation (PRF-1 family)') and consistent with mapping-critic F-3 (theorem obligations deferred to the theorem-design stage). The correspondence has four parts: (a)-(b) soundness (every outcome of the function is a step), (c) completeness (every step is realized by some function outcome), and (d) partial-completeness (function partiality none occurs exactly when the relation admits no step). Part (d) makes the partial-execution convention (Option none = partial execution for out-of-domain states, not an error; PTX-XOR-SEM1-052/053/054) precise with respect to the relation.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: (a) If execXorB32 s i returns some (ExecOutcome.executed s'), then XorB32Step s i s'. (b) If execXorB32 s i returns some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s'), then XorB32Step s i s'. (c) If XorB32Step s i s', then there exists an outcome o with execXorB32 s i = some o and o is either ExecOutcome.executed s' or ExecOutcome.guardFalse s'. (d) execXorB32 s i = none if and only if there is no state s' with XorB32Step s i s'.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem exec_sound_executed
    (s : MachineState) (i : XorB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (h : execXorB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) :
    XorB32Step s i s'

theorem exec_sound_guardFalse
    (s : MachineState) (i : XorB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (h : execXorB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')) :
    XorB32Step s i s'

theorem step_complete
    (s : MachineState) (i : XorB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (h : XorB32Step s i s') :
    Exists fun (o : ExecOutcome) =>
      execXorB32 s i = some o /\
      (o = ExecOutcome.executed s' \/ o = ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')

theorem step_partial_complete
    (s : MachineState) (i : XorB32Instruction) :
    execXorB32 s i = none <->
      not (Exists fun (s' : MachineState) => XorB32Step s i s')
hypotheses: Parts (a), (b), (d) quantify over arbitrary states and instructions; no additional preconditions are added.
Part (c) takes h : XorB32Step s i s' and concludes the existence of a corresponding function outcome.
theorem_obligations.conclusion: The four stated equivalences/implications between execXorB32 and XorB32Step.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Design dependency PTX-XOR-SEM1-063 (D-25 relational representation; relation/function correspondence is a theorem-stage obligation in the PRF-1 family); design dependency PTX-XOR-SEM1-064 (two-case outcome, no error constructor); DERIVED exclusive-or semantics PTX-XOR-SEM1-033, guard-true behavior PTX-XOR-SEM1-034, and guard-false state effect PTX-XOR-SEM1-035 (source-resolved via PTX-9.3-XOR-031/032). Partiality convention PTX-XOR-SEM1-052/053/054 (no invented error/UB; Option none is partial execution). Source evidence: PTX-9.3-XOR-005, PTX-9.3-XOR-031, PTX-9.3-XOR-032.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable witnesses for every part exist among the executable examples: part (b) via the @p with p = false example (guardFalse outcome; also a guardFalse step), part (a) via the aliasing d == a example (executed outcome; also an executed step), part (c) via both of those steps, and part (d) via the partial-execution example (missing source register yields none and no step). The conclusions are not elements of the hypotheses; each direction requires unfolding the definitions of both the function and the relation and is the substantive bridge deferred by the Lean file.
strength_risks: Part (d) must not be misread as asserting totality over all states; none for out-of-domain states is partiality (PTX-XOR-SEM1-052/053/054; risk R-2).

The relation omits the none partial case (it relates only complete executions); this is a mapping decision consistent with D-25 (mapping-critic F-3) and the correspondence makes it precise rather than hiding it.
The reviewer should confirm the four statements add no unapproved preconditions and use exactly the constructors of ExecOutcome.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: All four parts unfold execXorB32 and XorB32Step and case-split on evalGuard (Option Bool: none/some false/some true) and, where the executed branch is reached, on evalSource for i.a and then for i.b (Option B32). Part (a): with h, the evalGuard match took the some true branch and both evalSource matches the some va / some vb branches; instantiate the executed constructor. Part (b): the evalGuard match took the some false branch; instantiate the guardFalse constructor (note ExecOutcome.guardFalse s' forces s' = s). Part (c): case on the step constructor; for guardFalse, hguard : evalGuard = some false gives the guardFalse outcome; for executed, hguard, ha, and hb give the executed outcome with o = ExecOutcome.executed s'. Part (d): forward by cases on evalGuard/evalSource; reverse by showing each constructor would contradict execXorB32 = none.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-1 family (determinism and relation/function correspondence); XorB32-v1.lean lines 305-316.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the exclusive-or fidelity property: when the guard is true, the destination is a register r, and both sources resolve in the pre-instruction state s, the value written to r equals the bitwise exclusive-or of the values read from the two sources. This is the Semantics line 'd = a ^ b;' (PTX-9.3-XOR-005; SOURCE_FACT PTX-XOR-SEM1-032) and the derived exclusive-or semantics PTX-XOR-SEM1-033 (bitwise exclusive-or over the 32-bit untyped .b32 value domain; no arithmetic, truncation, or rounding). Because the source values are read from the pre-instruction state s (not from any post-update state), the statement also subsumes the read-before-write aliasing behavior PTX-XOR-SEM1-065: when i.a or i.b aliases the destination r, the values va/vb are the pre-update values of r, and the destination receives the exclusive-or of those pre-update values, matching the aliasing behavior demonstrated by the executable examples (d == a with r1 = 5, r2 = 3 gives r1 becomes 6; d == a == b with r1 = 5 gives r1 becomes 0). The exact formal statement is the semantic-phase matter OQ-8 / PTX-XOR-SEM1-072; this is the proposed formalization for theorem-strength review.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s, instruction i, register r, and B32 values va, vb: if the complete guard expression evaluates true in s, i.d is the register destination r, evalSource s i.a = some va, and evalSource s i.b = some vb (both sources resolve in the pre-instruction state s), then execXorB32 s i returns the executed outcome with some post-state s' and s'.valueRegs r = some (xorValue va vb). The equality pins the written value to the bitwise exclusive-or of the values read from the pre-instruction state, which is exactly the exclusive-or rule and the read-before-write aliasing behavior.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execXorB32_xor_fidelity
    (s : MachineState) (i : XorB32Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : B32)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true)
    (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r)
    (ha : evalSource s i.a = some va)
    (hb : evalSource s i.b = some vb) :
    Exists fun (s' : MachineState) =>
      execXorB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') /\
      s'.valueRegs r = some (xorValue va vb)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true (the complete guard expression is true, including the unguarded case)
hd : i.d = Destination.reg r (the destination is the register r; the bit-bucket destination is handled by PTX-XOR-THM-005)
ha : evalSource s i.a = some va (the first source resolves in the pre-instruction state s; va is the pre-update value)
hb : evalSource s i.b = some vb (the second source resolves in the pre-instruction state s; vb is the pre-update value)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Exists s' : MachineState, execXorB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') /\ s'.valueRegs r = some (xorValue va vb), i.e. the value written to r equals the bitwise exclusive-or of the values read from the two sources.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: SOURCE_FACT PTX-XOR-SEM1-032 (Semantics 'd = a ^ b;', PTX-9.3-XOR-005); DERIVED exclusive-or semantics PTX-XOR-SEM1-033 (grounded in PTX-9.3-XOR-002/004/005/021/023); DERIVED guard-true behavior PTX-XOR-SEM1-034; DERIVED source read PTX-XOR-SEM1-036; DERIVED destination write PTX-XOR-SEM1-038; DERIVED read-before-write PTX-XOR-SEM1-065; OPEN_QUESTION PTX-XOR-SEM1-072 (OQ-8: exact Lean statement of the exclusive-or fidelity candidate obligation PRF-7).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: the executable examples 5 ^ 3 = 6, 0xFFFFFFFF ^ 0 = 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFF0000 ^ 0x00FF00FF = 0xFF0000FF, the aliasing d == a example (r1 becomes 5 ^ 3 = 6), and the self-inverse aliasing d == a == b example (r1 becomes 5 ^ 5 = 0). The conclusion (the written value is exactly xorValue va vb) is not an element of the hypotheses; it pins the destination write to the exclusive-or of the pre-state source reads and distinguishes exclusive-or semantics from copy semantics, any other transformation, truncation, or read-after-write semantics.
strength_risks: The equality s'.valueRegs r = some (xorValue va vb) relies on xorValue being the bitwise exclusive-or over the 32-bit domain (the exclusive-or rule d = a ^ b; PTX-XOR-SEM1-032/033). The statement is written so that any faithful implementation of xorValue satisfies it; the reviewer should keep the exclusive-or-fidelity dependency explicit.
The theorem must keep va and vb defined from the pre-instruction state s (never from the post-state s'), or the read-before-write content (PTX-XOR-SEM1-065) would be lost.
The theorem does not assert behavior for missing registers; those are out-of-domain partiality (PTX-XOR-SEM1-052/053/054; risk R-2).
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execXorB32; with hguard the evalGuard match selects the some true branch; with ha and hb the two evalSource matches select some va and some vb; the result is some (ExecOutcome.executed (updateDestination s i.d (xorValue va vb))). With hd : i.d = Destination.reg r, unfold updateDestination and simplify the valueRegs update function (fun r' => if r' == r then some (xorValue va vb) else s.valueRegs r') with the DecidableEq of RegId to conclude s'.valueRegs r = some (xorValue va vb). The aliasing cases i.a = SourceOperand.reg r and/or i.b = SourceOperand.reg r follow with ha/hb : evalSource s (SourceOperand.reg r) = some va/vb and evalSource unfolding to s.valueRegs r = some va/vb, i.e. the pre-update values.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-7 (exclusive-or fidelity: the value written equals the bitwise exclusive-or of the values read, 'd = a ^ b;', PTX-9.3-XOR-005); read-before-write aspect of PTX-XOR-SEM1-065.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the destination-only update / frame property over the execution relation: when a step executes with a register destination r, the only value register that may change is r; every other value register and every predicate register is unchanged. This is the relational frame obligation (architecture PRF-2; semantics future topic PRF-2) grounded in DERIVED claims PTX-XOR-SEM1-038 (only the destination register is updated) and PTX-XOR-SEM1-039 (write locality: no memory, special-register, carry-flag, status-register, or condition-code component is written by the bounded base xor.b32). The statement is made over the bounded model (value-register file plus predicate-register file) and retains the documented negative-evidence caveat: the bounded model contains no carry-flag/status components, and the absence of such writes is absence-based negative evidence (PTX-XOR-SEM1-039/052/053/054; risk R-1), not an affirmative NVIDIA enumeration; the frame claim must not be cited as an explicit NVIDIA statement about components outside the model.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s, instruction i, related state s', and register r: if XorB32Step s i s' and i.d is the register destination r, then (1) every value register r' different from r has the same value in s' as in s; and (2) every predicate register p has the same value in s' as in s. The theorem holds in both the executed and the guard-false cases (in the guard-false case s' = s, so the frame is trivially satisfied; the executed case is the content).
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem xorB32Step_destination_only_frame
    (s : MachineState) (i : XorB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (r : RegId)
    (hstep : XorB32Step s i s')
    (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) :
    (forall (r' : RegId), r' != r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r') /\
    (forall (p : PredId), s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p)
hypotheses: hstep : XorB32Step s i s' (the relation admits a step from s on i to s')
hd : i.d = Destination.reg r (the destination is the register r)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: (forall r', r' != r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r') /\ (forall p, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: DERIVED claims PTX-XOR-SEM1-038 (state write: destination register d updated with the bitwise exclusive-or of the values read from a and b; the source states no other register write) and PTX-XOR-SEM1-039 (write locality: only the destination update required by the bounded semantics; no memory/special-register/carry/status component written); PTX-XOR-SEM1-060 (minimal state pair). Source evidence: PTX-9.3-XOR-002, PTX-9.3-XOR-004, PTX-9.3-XOR-005. The absence of carry/status writes is NEGATIVE evidence (PTX-XOR-SEM1-039/052/053/054; risk R-1).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: the executable example with r1 = 1, r2 = 2 and updateDestination (Destination.reg r1) (mkB32 100) shows r1 becomes 100 while r2 remains 2 and the predicate file is untouched. The conclusion (all other value registers and all predicates preserved) is not an element of the hypotheses; it is the frame content and distinguishes destination-only semantics from any semantics writing additional state.
strength_risks: Risk R-1 (PTX-XOR-SEM1-039/052/053/054): the theorem must be stated over the bounded model only and must not be cited as an explicit NVIDIA statement that 'no carry flag / status register is written'. The absence-based caveat must remain traceable until final acceptance.

The theorem does not assert the value written to r itself (that is PTX-XOR-THM-003); a reviewer should ensure no attempt to strengthen this theorem into an assertion about components outside the model.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case on hstep. The guardFalse constructor gives s' = s, so both conjuncts are by reflexivity. The executed constructor gives s' = updateDestination s i.d (xorValue va vb); with hd : i.d = Destination.reg r, unfold updateDestination: the valueRegs function becomes fun r' => if r' == r then some (xorValue va vb) else s.valueRegs r'. Use by_cases (r' == r) on the DecidableEq of RegId to prove r' != r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r'; predicate registers are untouched because only the valueRegs field is updated in the record (predRegs equality by record simplification).
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-2 (destination-only update / frame), with negative-evidence caveat from risk R-1.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the bit-bucket discard property over the execution relation: when the destination is the bit bucket '_', a step changes no value register and the whole state is unchanged (s' = s). This corresponds to semantics future topic PRF-3. The obligation retains the documented strength caveat: the no-write consequence is supported only to the strength of the general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule (SOURCE_FACT PTX-XOR-SEM1-011 / fragment PTX-9.3-XOR-016; open question PTX-XOR-SEM1-067/AMB-3, bundle GAP-2); the scalar xor.b32 section does not demonstrate the bit-bucket form, so the theorem must not be presented as a xor.b32-specific explicit source fact (mapping-critic F-2).
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s, instruction i, and related state s': if XorB32Step s i s' and i.d is the bit bucket Destination.bitBucket, then s' = s: the computed value is discarded and no value register or predicate register changes. The strength of this claim is limited to the general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule (PTX-XOR-SEM1-011/067).
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem xorB32Step_bit_bucket_preserves_state
    (s : MachineState) (i : XorB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (hstep : XorB32Step s i s')
    (hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket) :
    s' = s
hypotheses: hstep : XorB32Step s i s' (the relation admits a step from s on i to s')
hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket (the destination is the bit bucket '_')
theorem_obligations.conclusion: s' = s (the related state is exactly the input state; the result is discarded).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: SOURCE_FACT PTX-XOR-SEM1-011 (general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule: for some instructions a bit bucket '_' may be used in place of a destination register; PTX-9.3-XOR-016); OPEN_QUESTION PTX-XOR-SEM1-067 (whether '_' is permitted for the scalar xor.b32 form; AMB-3, GAP-2); design dependency PTX-XOR-SEM1-064 (execution outcome representation).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: the executable example with the bit bucket destination keeps r1 at 1 (no value register written), demonstrating the no-write behavior; a guard-false step with bit bucket destination also satisfies s' = s. The conclusion s' = s is not an element of the hypotheses; it is the discard content and distinguishes the bit-bucket destination from the register destination (PTX-XOR-THM-003/004).
strength_risks: Risk R-3 (AMB-3 / PTX-XOR-SEM1-067 / mapping-critic F-2): the theorem must not be presented as xor.b32-specific explicit NVIDIA behavior; it is supported only to the strength of the general section 9.2 rule. PRF-3 strength must not exceed this.

If the theorem-strength review decides the bit-bucket constructor should be deferred until the scalar applicability question (PTX-XOR-SEM1-067) is resolved, this obligation is removed or weakened accordingly; the current statement is faithful to the Gate-C-approved Lean mapping, which materializes the constructor at candidate strength (mapping-critic F-2).
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case on hstep. The guardFalse constructor gives s' = s directly. The executed constructor gives s' = updateDestination s i.d (xorValue va vb); with hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket, unfold updateDestination: the bitBucket branch returns s, so s' = s; simp.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-3 (bit-bucket discard), with AMB-3 strength caveat.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish that when the complete guard expression evaluates false, the instruction is not executed and the machine state is unchanged. This is the guard-false frame property (semantics future topic PRF-4), grounded in the DERIVED_INTERPRETATION PTX-XOR-SEM1-035, which is source-resolved via the official section 9.7.13.2 clause 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-XOR-031/032; SOURCE_FACT PTX-XOR-SEM1-028; derivation chain PTX-XOR-SEM1-031). It is NOT a human assumption and must never be presented as one. The functional form (a) states that the guard-false outcome carries exactly the input state, so no value-register or predicate-register component changes; it also entails that source operands are NOT read in this branch (the code returns before evaluating sources), matching the mapping decision confirmed at Gate C (mapping-critic F-4) and consistent with the approved 'do nothing' reading. The relational form (b) states the same over XorB32Step.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: (a) For every state s and instruction i, if evaluating the complete guard expression in s yields some false, then execXorB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s): the outcome is the guard-false outcome carrying exactly the input state, so no machine-state component changes and no source operand is read. (b) For every state s, instruction i, and related state s', if XorB32Step s i s' and evalGuard s i.guard = some false, then s' = s.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execXorB32_guard_false_preserves_state
    (s : MachineState) (i : XorB32Instruction)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) :
    execXorB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s)

theorem xorB32Step_guard_false_frame
    (s : MachineState) (i : XorB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (hstep : XorB32Step s i s')
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) :
    s' = s
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false (the complete guard expression evaluates false in s)
No source-resolution hypotheses are needed: the guard-false branch does not read source operands (this is part of the conclusion, not a precondition).
theorem_obligations.conclusion: (a) execXorB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s); consequently the carried state equals the input state and the instruction has no state effect. (b) XorB32Step s i s' with evalGuard = some false forces s' = s.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: DERIVED_INTERPRETATION PTX-XOR-SEM1-035 (guard-false state effect), source-resolved via SOURCE_FACT PTX-XOR-SEM1-028 (section 9.7.13.2 clause 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.', PTX-9.3-XOR-031/032) and the derivation chain PTX-XOR-SEM1-031; design dependency PTX-XOR-SEM1-064 (two-case outcome, guardFalse carries the unchanged state). Source-non-reading in the guard-false branch is the Gate-C-confirmed mapping decision (mapping-critic F-4).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: any state in which the referenced guard predicate is defined to false, or @!p with p true (the executable example @p with p = false keeps r1 at 5 demonstrates the behavior). The conclusion is not an element of the hypotheses; it pins the exact outcome constructor and the unchanged carried state, which is the semantic content of 'do nothing'.
strength_risks: The guard-false behavior must be presented as a DERIVED_INTERPRETATION from the explicit predication clause applied to xor.b32 (PTX-XOR-SEM1-035/031), never as an affirmative per-instruction SOURCE_FACT that the PTX xor section itself states this.
The theorem is stated over the bounded model state pair; it does not by itself assert anything about components outside the model (deferred property PTX-XOR-DEF-001).

Part (a)'s equality to ExecOutcome.guardFalse s (carrying exactly s) is a full state-preservation statement because guardFalse carries the whole MachineState and the only producer of guardFalse in execXorB32 is the unchanged input state.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Part (a): unfold execXorB32; with hguard the evalGuard match selects the some false branch, which returns some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s) directly; the source-evaluation branches are never reached, so no source-resolution case analysis is needed. Part (b): case on hstep; the executed constructor requires evalGuard = some true, which contradicts hguard (injectivity of some on Option Bool), so only the guardFalse constructor applies and s' = s.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-4 (guard-false frame); source-non-reading decision confirmed at Gate C.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the guard-behavior equivalence (semantics future topic PRF-5): on the approved well-formed lookup domain, an executed outcome occurs if and only if the complete guard expression evaluates true. This covers the no-guard, @p, and @!p cases uniformly through evalGuard and pins the outcome classification of execXorB32. It complements PTX-XOR-THM-006 (guard-false state preservation) by providing the reverse direction: an executed outcome implies the guard was true, so an instruction can never execute under a false complete guard. Because xor.b32 has two source operands, the source-resolution hypothesis requires both a and b to resolve when the guard is true. The supporting guard-evaluation lemmas pin the per-constructor behavior of evalGuard (unguarded = true; @p = predicate value; @!p = negation) per PTX-XOR-SEM1-022/037/044 and the general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-XOR-SEM1-029).
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s and instruction i, if the complete guard expression resolves in s to some b and, when b is true, both sources resolve in s, then there exists an executed outcome from execXorB32 s i if and only if b is true. Equivalently: execution happens exactly when the complete guard expression is true; when b is false the outcome is the guard-false outcome (and, by PTX-XOR-THM-006, the state is unchanged). Supporting lemmas: evalGuard s Guard.unguarded = some true; s.predRegs p = some true -> evalGuard s (Guard.atPos p) = some true; s.predRegs p = some false -> evalGuard s (Guard.atNeg p) = some true; s.predRegs p = some false -> evalGuard s (Guard.atPos p) = some false; s.predRegs p = some true -> evalGuard s (Guard.atNeg p) = some false.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem xorB32_executes_iff_guard_true
    (s : MachineState) (i : XorB32Instruction) (b : Bool)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some b)
    (hsources : b = true -> Exists fun (va : B32) => Exists fun (vb : B32) =>
        evalSource s i.a = some va /\ evalSource s i.b = some vb) :
    (Exists fun (s' : MachineState) =>
        execXorB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) <-> b = true

-- supporting guard-evaluation lemmas (per-constructor evalGuard behavior)
theorem evalGuard_unguarded_true
    (s : MachineState) : evalGuard s Guard.unguarded = some true

theorem evalGuard_atPos_true
    (s : MachineState) (p : PredId) (h : s.predRegs p = some true) :
    evalGuard s (Guard.atPos p) = some true

theorem evalGuard_atNeg_true_when_pred_false
    (s : MachineState) (p : PredId) (h : s.predRegs p = some false) :
    evalGuard s (Guard.atNeg p) = some true

theorem evalGuard_atPos_false
    (s : MachineState) (p : PredId) (h : s.predRegs p = some false) :
    evalGuard s (Guard.atPos p) = some false

theorem evalGuard_atNeg_false_when_pred_true
    (s : MachineState) (p : PredId) (h : s.predRegs p = some true) :
    evalGuard s (Guard.atNeg p) = some false
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some b (the complete guard expression resolves in s to b)
hsources : if b = true then both sources resolve in s: Exists va, Exists vb, evalSource s i.a = some va /\ evalSource s i.b = some vb
No additional guard or source preconditions.
theorem_obligations.conclusion: (Exists s', execXorB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) <-> b = true; plus the per-constructor evalGuard lemmas.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: SOURCE_FACT PTX-XOR-SEM1-022 (optional guard predicate @{!}p; instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally); SOURCE_FACT PTX-XOR-SEM1-029 (general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction', PTX-9.3-XOR-032); DERIVED PTX-XOR-SEM1-031 (derivation chain for xor.b32 guard behavior) and PTX-XOR-SEM1-034 (guard-true behavior); DERIVED PTX-XOR-SEM1-037 (guard predicate read); DERIVED PTX-XOR-SEM1-044 (PRE-5 guard well-typedness). Source evidence: PTX-9.3-XOR-017, PTX-9.3-XOR-018, PTX-9.3-XOR-031, PTX-9.3-XOR-032, PTX-9.3-XOR-033.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Both directions are non-trivial. Forward: with b = true and hsources, the code reaches the executed branch. Reverse: with b = false, the code returns guardFalse, so no executed outcome exists. There exist states satisfying the hypotheses for both values of b (e.g., @p with p true and with p false; the @!p with p = false executable example shows r1 becoming 5 ^ 3 = 6), and the theorem's biconditional is false if the outcome classification were wrong, so it is not vacuous. The supporting evalGuard lemmas pin the per-constructor guard evaluation and distinguish @p from @!p (opposite execution conditions; PTX-XOR-SEM1-022/037/044).
strength_risks: The theorem is a classification/guard-behavior statement, not a determinism claim; it must not be mistaken for PRF-1 (relational determinism, PTX-XOR-THM-001) or for the functional single-valuedness of execXorB32.

The hypothesis shape must match the well-formed lookup domain exactly; adding source-resolution hypotheses unconditionally (even when b = false) would be an unapproved strengthening and would make the reverse direction trivial in a different way.
The supporting lemmas are simple definitional statements; they must not be presented as deep semantic theorems, only as the per-constructor guard evaluation facts behind PRF-5.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execXorB32. Forward direction: assume b = true, use hsources to obtain va and vb; evalGuard gives some true, evalSource for i.a gives some va and for i.b gives some vb, so the result is some (ExecOutcome.executed _). Reverse direction: assume Exists s', execXorB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s'); the evalGuard match in execXorB32 must have taken the some true branch (the some false branch returns guardFalse and the none branch returns none), hence b = true (use hguard and injectivity of some). The supporting lemmas unfold evalGuard and evaluate the match on the constructor.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-5 (guard behavior: executes iff complete guard expression true, covering no-guard, @p, @!p uniformly).

deferred_properties.title: Whole-PTX frame claims about components outside the minimal state (carry flags, status/condition-code registers, memory, shared, special registers)
deferred_properties.description: The bounded model is the minimal approved pair (value-register file, predicate-register file). Statements such as 'xor.b32 writes no carry flag or status register' are absence-based negative evidence (PTX-XOR-SEM1-039/052/053/054; risk R-1), not affirmative NVIDIA enumeration. No theorem is proposed over components outside the bounded model; PTX-XOR-THM-004 is stated strictly over the model and retains the caveat.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Requires a broader machine model outside this bounded unit; negative evidence must not be presented as an affirmative theorem.

deferred_properties.title: Scalar xor.b32-specific bit-bucket demonstration (PTX-XOR-SEM1-067 / AMB-3)
deferred_properties.description: PTX-XOR-THM-005 states the no-write consequence at the strength of the general section 9.2 rule (PTX-XOR-SEM1-011/067). Whether the scalar xor.b32 section itself demonstrates the bit-bucket form remains an open question (AMB-3, GAP-2; mapping-critic F-2). Strengthening the bit-bucket theorem into an explicit xor.b32-specific source claim is deferred pending official evidence.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Open question PTX-XOR-SEM1-067; scalar xor.b32-specific demonstration absent.

deferred_properties.title: Constant-immediate source permissibility (PTX-XOR-SEM1-066 / AMB-2)
deferred_properties.description: Whether the source operands a and/or b of xor.b32 may be constant immediates is not explicitly evidenced in the xor section for the .b32 form (PTX-XOR-SEM1-066/010, bundle GAP-1, AMB-2); the xor section's own immediate example is in the .b16 form (xor.b16 d,x,0x0001;, PTX-9.3-XOR-009) and sibling-family .b32 immediate examples are recorded with do_not_infer: true (PTX-9.3-XOR-011/012). The Lean candidate models the sources as register-only (SourceOperand.reg is the only constructor; no immediate constructor is introduced). Any theorem about which source forms are legal, or about immediate-source behavior, is deferred. This affects static well-formedness of programs only and does not change the state transition of a given legal instruction.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Open question PTX-XOR-SEM1-066; sibling-family immediates recorded with do_not_infer: true; static well-formedness, outside executable-semantics scope.

deferred_properties.title: Version and target gating theorems (PTX-XOR-SEM1-045/048/049/050/051)
deferred_properties.description: Base xor (and therefore the bounded base xor.b32 form) is introduced in PTX ISA 1.0 (PTX-XOR-SEM1-045/048/050) and is supported on all target architectures (PTX-XOR-SEM1-049/051, directly evidenced in the xor section itself; no target-set gap exists for xor.b32). These are static validation-layer obligations (architecture VAL-5/VAL-6), not executable state-transition behavior; the Lean candidate does not model version/target metadata. Theorems about version/target validity are deferred to the validation layer.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Version/target metadata is outside the executable mapping scope of the bounded unit.

deferred_properties.title: Behavior on out-of-domain states (missing guard predicate or source register)
deferred_properties.description: For states in which a referenced guard predicate or source register is not defined, execXorB32 returns none. This is PARTIAL execution for out-of-domain states, not an error, trap, undefined behavior, or implementation-defined behavior (PTX-XOR-SEM1-052/053/054; risk R-2). No theorem will be stated about 'error' behavior, and none must never be interpreted as an approved error. The partial-completeness correspondence (PTX-XOR-THM-002 part (d)) makes this convention precise: none occurs exactly when the relation admits no step.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: The approved semantics fixes behavior only for the well-formed domain; out-of-domain behavior is a partiality convention, not a semantic property.

deferred_properties.title: Error / undefined / implementation-defined behavior claims (PTX-XOR-SEM1-052/053/054)
deferred_properties.description: No explicit error, trap, undefined-behavior, or implementation-defined-behavior clause for xor (or xor.b32) was found in the evidence (bundle GAP-4); none is invented. Whether the absence means no such behaviors exist is an open question (PTX-XOR-SEM1-052/053/054). Any future claim of such behavior requires official evidence and is deferred.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Absence of evidence; no behavior invented; any positive claim would require new official evidence.

deferred_properties.title: Predicate register value-domain encoding (PTX-XOR-SEM1-069 / OQ-5)
deferred_properties.description: The exact Lean encoding of the 1-bit predicate register value domain (predicate registers are 1-bit, PTX-9.3-XOR-023) is a Lean-mapping decision for a later phase (PTX-XOR-SEM1-069/OQ-5; mapping-critic F-1). The Lean candidate uses Bool for predicate values (design D-13); the encoding decision itself is not a theorem obligation. If the encoding changes, the guard-evaluation lemmas in PTX-XOR-THM-007 must be re-verified against the new encoding.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Open question PTX-XOR-SEM1-069; encoding is a Lean-mapping decision, not a semantic property.

deferred_properties.title: Operand-typing formulation (PTX-XOR-SEM1-071 / AMB-4 / OQ-7)
deferred_properties.description: The exact formulation of the family size-matching rule 'The size of the operands must match, but not necessarily the type.' (PTX-9.3-XOR-006) combined with the bit-size compatibility rule (PTX-9.3-XOR-022) for xor.b32 operand typing (e.g., whether a register declared .u32, .s32, or .f32 is an acceptable operand for instruction type .b32) is not resolved (PTX-XOR-SEM1-071, AMB-4, GAP-5). This affects static well-formedness of programs only and does not change the state transition of a given legal instruction. Theorems about the typing relation are deferred to a static well-formedness layer.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Open question PTX-XOR-SEM1-071; static well-formedness, outside executable-semantics scope.

known_risks.description: Negative-evidence caveat for the frame/no-carry statements (PTX-XOR-SEM1-039/052/053/054). PTX-XOR-THM-004 and any frame reasoning must be stated over the bounded model and must not cite 'no carry flag / status register is written' as an explicit NVIDIA statement. Caveat retained in PTX-XOR-THM-004 and deferred property PTX-XOR-DEF-001; must remain traceable until final acceptance.

Option none is partiality, not an error (PTX-XOR-SEM1-052/053/054). All faithfulness theorems quantify over the approved well-formed lookup domain via lookup-success hypotheses (PTX-XOR-THM-003/007 shape); none must never be interpreted as an approved error/trap/UB behavior.

Bit-bucket strength is limited to the general section 9.2 rule (AMB-3 / PTX-XOR-SEM1-067 / mapping-critic F-2). PTX-XOR-THM-005 retains the strength caveat and is not presented as xor.b32-specific explicit behavior.

Register-only source: the Lean candidate introduces no immediate constructor (AMB-2 / PTX-XOR-SEM1-066). Any theorem about immediate-source behavior or immediate legality is deferred (PTX-XOR-DEF-003); the obligations never quantify over a SourceOperand.imm form because none exists.

Theorem statements in this specification are Lean sketches, not compiled Lean. Independent theorem-strength review (Gate THEOREM_STRENGTH) must validate each statement's hypotheses, non-vacuity, and faithfulness before any proof file is written.

PRF-6 vacuity risk: result-domain membership is adopted as a VAL-style definitional well-formedness obligation (PTX-XOR-VAL-002), following the disposition recorded in semantics PRF-6 (architecture A-10). The theorem-strength reviewer should confirm the disposition; no semantic proof obligation is proposed for PRF-6.

traceability_summary.determinism_note: PRF-1 relational determinism is proposed as PTX-XOR-THM-001 over the relational inductive XorB32Step (a Prop relation, not a function), per design D-25 / PTX-XOR-SEM1-063; it is non-vacuous because the relation is not definitionally a function. A statement that the total function execXorB32 'returns one value' would be a trivial fact of function application and is explicitly NOT proposed (compliance_notes item 3). The substantive function/relation bridge is PTX-XOR-THM-002 (XorB32-v1.lean lines 305-316).
